related_evidence.description: Publication of the Phase 2 readout in progressive supranuclear palsy confirming clinical futility of tilavonemab despite an acceptable safety profile.

Systems pharmacology modeling analysis exploring the clinical failure of anti-tau antibodies including tilavonemab, pointing to target engagement not translating to downstream slowing of neurodegeneration.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence robustly demonstrates that tilavonemab (ABBV-8E12) lacks therapeutic efficacy in slowing clinical or cognitive decline. In the Phase 2 early Alzheimer's disease trial (NCT02880956), despite clear biomarker evidence of target engagement (reductions in CSF free tau and increases in plasma total tau), there was no significant improvement on the primary endpoint (CDR-SB) or secondary clinical measures. This failure pattern mirrored a parallel Phase 2 trial for progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) that was terminated early for futility. Consequently, AbbVie has terminated all associated extension studies for both indications, solidifying the conclusion that targeting the N-terminus of tau with tilavonemab is not a viable disease-modifying strategy.
discrepancies: None. The document accurately reflects the clinical registry and publication record, which confirm the drug successfully engaged its target but completely failed on all primary and secondary efficacy endpoints.
